CONTEXT.goal: Apply the remaining OTA query instrumentation so live runs can distinguish API-only accept, API+DOM merge, and DOM-only fallback, while collapsing duplicate source-count handling.
CONTEXT.summary: The previous PoC reclassified OTA query to bridge-candidate, but the code still lacked runtime counters and UI-visible instrumentation for the three fetch routes.
constraints: Keep the change minimal and localized to OTA query measurement.
Do not widen DOM fallback behavior or touch write/apply logic.
Prefer integrating duplicate source-count logic instead of adding parallel code paths.

symptoms: OTA query route classification had been verified in a harness but not instrumented for live session frequency tracking.
UI status text recomputed source counts ad hoc instead of consuming the fetch-layer result.

ROOT_CAUSE.summary: The fetch layer returned only rows, so route choice and source mix stayed implicit and duplicated across consumers instead of being recorded once and reused.
evidence: Before this change, `loadInventory` recalculated API/DOM source counts directly from rows and had no access to route-level counters.
Adding fetch-layer meta and a shared source-summary helper let the UI and test consume the same measured result.

ACTION.summary: Added provider-level fetch instrumentation and shared source-summary helpers in `pms.fetch`, wired `sheetScanner.entry` to reuse the measured meta, and extended the existing OTA PoC to validate all three routes plus cumulative counters.
changes: Recorded provider fetch outcomes for `api_only_accept`, `api_dom_merge`, `dom_only_fallback`, `api_only_insufficient`, and `api_error_no_dom`.
Stored the last provider-row meta in `src/sheetScanner.entry.js` and rendered current route plus session counters from the fetch-layer instrumentation.
Extended `tests/regression_ota_dom_fallback_poc.mjs` to verify API-only, degraded merge, and DOM-only fallback scenarios with route counters.
Updated the architecture document to reflect that runtime instrumentation now exists.

OUTCOME.summary: OTA query now exposes reusable live-route instrumentation, and duplicated API/DOM source counting was integrated into one fetch-layer helper.
verified_facts: The fetch layer now records per-provider route counters and last-event meta.
The UI status line now consumes the fetch-layer meta instead of recomputing source counts separately.
The existing OTA PoC now verifies all three route classes and cumulative counters for both providers.
remaining_risks: Live production frequency still depends on collecting enough real sessions after deployment.

use_when: A fetch path needs live-route instrumentation and multiple consumers currently recompute the same source summary.
You need to distinguish API-only success, API+fallback merge, and DOM-only fallback without changing the business behavior.
avoid_when: The fetch layer is not the single source of truth for the returned rows or different consumers intentionally need divergent summaries.
REUSE_RULE.fallback: If a route still cannot be distinguished after helper extraction, record the raw branch decision in the fetch layer first and only then update downstream UI/report consumers.
